name: Dominant Indices
description: You are given a rooted undirected tree consisting of $$$n$$$ vertices. Vertex $$$1$$$ is the root. Let's denote a depth array of vertex $$$x$$$ as an infinite sequence $$$[d_{x, 0}, d_{x, 1}, d_{x, 2}, \dots]$$$, where $$$d_{x, i}$$$ is the number of vertices $$$y$$$ such that both conditions hold: $$$x$$$ is an ancestor of $$$y$$$; the simple path from $$$x$$$ to $$$y$$$ traverses exactly $$$i$$$ edges. The dominant index of a depth array of vertex $$$x$$$ (or, shortly, the dominant index of vertex $$$x$$$) is an index $$$j$$$ such that: for every $$$k \lt j$$$, $$$d_{x, k} \lt d_{x, j}$$$; for every $$$k \gt j$$$, $$$d_{x, k} \le d_{x, j}$$$. For every vertex in the tree calculate its dominant index .
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^6$$$) — the number of vertices in a tree. Then $$$n - 1$$$ lines follow, each containing two integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ ($$$1 \le x, y \le n$$$, $$$x \ne y$$$). This line denotes an edge of the tree. It is guaranteed that these edges form a tree.
output_specification: Output $$$n$$$ numbers. $$$i$$$-th number should be equal to the dominant index of vertex $$$i$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1009F — Dominant Indices [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
